Harry Chapman Pincher, a former *Daily Express* defense correspondent, was renowned for securing scoops through his ability to cultivate high-level contacts via social settings like lunching and game shooting. 

After his retirement, he published books alleging that Britain's security services had been penetrated by spies at the highest levels.

The council has voted to urgently dismantle a dangerous section of a Grade II listed pier to prevent further collapse. The work is expected to take three weeks, with parts of the structure being saved and stored for future use. While up to £650,000 has been allocated, the final cost remains uncertain due to the hazardous nature of the project.

The world's largest clothing retailer, Inditex, reported an 8% increase in net earnings to €1.26bn for the first half of the year, driven by strong sales and international expansion. The group's growth was fueled by significant investments in digital technology and the expansion of its online presence across 40 countries. This strong performance sets the company apart from competitors as it continues to integrate its brick-and-mortar and online retail channels.

Kazuyoshi Miura, known as "King Kazu," has signed a contract extension with his second-division club that will keep him playing past his 49th birthday, making his professional career span over 30 years. The 55-year-old veteran, who began his career in Brazil at age 15, remains motivated to contribute everything he has, holding the record as Japan's oldest scorer while aiming to continue his remarkable longevity in the sport.

Cambridgeshire Police have arrested a 64-year-old man after human bones were found during a 13-day search on land in Ramsey, which reopened the 1990 disappearance of Andrew Bedford as a murder inquiry. Detectives believe Mr Bedford was shot with a shotgun in September 1990, and now the remains will undergo DNA testing to confirm his identity. The investigation continues as police appeal for additional information from locals to help bring resolution to the case.

Harry Chapman Pincher, a former defence correspondent for the Daily Express, became renowned for his investigative journalism and ability to recall minute details without taking notes. After retiring, he authored books alleging that Britain's security services had been penetrated by top-level spies. His unorthodox methods, including cultivating sources over lunch at a French restaurant bugged by MI5 and the KGB, allowed him to expose sensitive information about Britain's atomic weapons programme and high-level government secrets.

The Scottish government has intervened in East Dunbartonshire Council's proposal to close St Joseph's Primary in Milngavie, citing concerns over inaccurate information in the consultation process. While the council plans to merge St Joseph's with St Andrew's Primary in Bearsden into a new £9 million building, the government's review highlights procedural flaws and unaddressed concerns from Education Scotland. DUP MP Ian Paisley has criticized Taoiseach Enda Kenny’s recent comments regarding a potential Irish unity referendum, which Kenny suggested could triggered due to Brexit, as "mischievous." Paisley argued that the prospect of a border poll is unrealistic given previous government rulings. Sinn Féin president Gerry Adams, however, welcomed Kenny's remarks as creating a "greater opportunity" to achieve a united Ireland. Meanwhile, other unionist politicians dismissed the comments as a distraction from the urgent need to address Northern Ireland's economic future post-BEU.

The National Museum of the Royal Navy has proposed moving the "Yomper" statue from Eastney to Portsmouth, as part of a £13m project to relocate the Royal Marines Museum, sparking opposition from local campaigners. The statue, which depicts a Royal Marine from the 1882 conflict, has been a local landmark since 1992 and is viewed by supporters as a vital part of Eastney's heritage. Museum officials argue the move would expose the statue to significantly more visitors, while opponents insist it belongs in its original outdoor setting.

Following a deadly terrorist attack in Tunisia, which claimed by ISIS, causing significant loss of life, President Francois Hollande expressed deep sadness and the Prime Minister admitted security shortcomings.

The attack, which targeted foreign tourists and led to multiple arrests, has prompted a massive anti-terrorism march and security concerns regarding the reopening of the Bardo museum.

The incident has shaken the nation, which has been under threat since the Arab Spring uprising.

World number two and snooker player Neil Bingham has questioning his participation in this upcoming tournament due to his wife's pregnancy. He remains uncertain whether she will stay in labor or if the birth occurs before his scheduled match against Joe Perry. He plans to consult with his wife to decide his next move.

Tiger Woods missed the cut at Torrey Pines after shooting a second-round 72, marking a frustrating return to competitive play following a long injury layoff. Other high-profile players, including Jason Day, Dustin Johnson, and Jimmy Walker, also failed to make the cut. Meanwhile, overnight leader Rose currently holds the lead at eight under par.

Wasps secured a crucial victory against Worcester, earning five bonus points to guarantee their play-off place while the Warriors remain in contention for European qualification. The match was characterized by disciplinary issues, with Bryce Heem sent off for Wasps and Matt Mullan sin-binned for Worcester, as both teams displayed strong defensive efforts and competitive spirit. Wasps director of rugby Dai Young praised his team's resilience and quality, while Worcester's Gary Gold highlighted his side's character and improved performance despite the loss.

South Africa’s government has proposed a minimum wage to combat income poverty, while critics warn that the rate could potentially increase unemployment because employers might not be able to afford higher labor costs. The proposed figure has drawn mixed reactions, with some experts arguing it is insufficient to sustain a household while political parties debate its impact on business versus workers. The government aims to finalize the national minimum wage within two years, despite ongoing concerns about economic stability and credit ratings.

Retired General David Petraeus warns that "industrial-strength" extremists like IS cannot be defeated by military force alone, emphasizing the need for a political solution and Sunni support to stabilize Iraq. He views the recent loss of Ramadi as a significant setback but remains confident the city will be retaken quickly, while stressing that the Iraqi military must refine its strategy to ultimately succeed against the group.

Hong Kong regulators fined RBS following the conviction of former trader Shirlina Tsang for fraud involving falsified emerging markets trade records. While the regulator noted "significant weaknesses" in the bank's internal controls, the fine was mitigated due to RBS's prompt cooperation with authorities once the illegal activity was discovered.

The upcoming football tournament in France will feature 24 teams competing in a new expanded format to determine the champion. While Germany and Spain are considered the favorites, France faces the pressure of hosting amidst national recovery.

The tournament features a group stage where the top teams advance to a knockout format, with the final scheduled to take place in Paris.

ID Systems, an industrial and commercial utilities company based in Glasgow, is expanding its workforce by creating new jobs in Glasgow and Lancashire. This growth is supported by a loan and equity investment from UKSE, the Tata Steel subsidiary, which will help fund the company's strategy and enable the creation of a new senior management team. The expansion follows ID Systems securing long-term projects, including off-site manufacturing for wastewater pumping stations, and the company aims to more than double its current staff of 80.

Martyn Irvine made history by becoming the first Irish cyclist in 117 years to win a world track title, adding a silver in the points race at the World Championships in Belarus. Despite suffering a fractured hip in Taiwan shortly after, he remarkably regained fitness to win European bronze and a World Cup event in Manchester, earning him the BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year award.

The government has "called in" proposals to shut St Joseph's Primary in Milngavie near Glasgow. The council plans to build a new denominational primary in nearby Bearsden - replacing both St Joseph's and the school on the site at present. Parents at St Joseph's and the Catholic Church have been fighting the plan. East Dunbartonshire Council plans to merge St Joseph's Primary with St Andrew's Primary in neighbouring Bearsden. The merged school would be sited in a new building on the current St Andrew's Primary School site. When the Scottish government calls in any proposal to close

The Care Inspectorate gave Nithsdale House in Glasgow a rating of one, the lowest possible, after an unannounced inspection in February citing serious concerns about the quality of care, staffing, and management. The agency also inspected Drumpellier Lodge, which received a rating of two, the second lowest, due to unmet improvement requirements and ongoing issues with care and leadership. Both facilities have been ordered to make urgent improvements, with warnings that further action will be taken if significant progress is not demonstrated.

The 22-year-old has signed a one-year contract, joining defender Craig Barr and striker Mark Stewart at the Scottish Championship club. Johnston came through Kilmarnock's youth ranks to make the Premiership side's first team. But he moved to Kirkcaldy last summer and played 34 times. Barr, 30, had been at Stark's Park for three seasons after leaving Airdrieonians and played 17 times as Rovers dropped to League One, while the 29-year-old Stewart joined at Derry City and scored five times in 36 appearances

Identical twins Tom and Sam have made nine combined Premiership appearances for Sale Sharks, becoming only the fourth set of twins to play side-by-side in the league. Both players, who feature for England Under-20, are viewed as key components of the club's strategy to develop academy talent for the first team. Their contributions include Tom setting a record as the Sharks' youngest Premiership try scorer.

The United Arab Emirates para-athlete Abdullah Hayayei was tragically when after a incident at Newham Leisure Centre during training for the World Para-athletics Championships in London. The IPC confirmed that the throwing cage collapsed on the athlete's head, and the incident was witnessed by some of Hayayei's team-mates and UAE staff. The Metropolitan Police said emergency services "were called shortly after 17:00hrs on Tuesday" to reports of a seriously injured man at Newham Leisure Centre.

TRNSMT, Scotland's newest music festival, is launching at Glasgow Green this weekend, headlined by Radiohead, Kasabian, and Biffy Clyro, as a replacement for the suspended T in the Park. Organizers DF Concerts introduced the event following a challenging period for T in the Park, which faced severe criticism over safety issues and logistical failures in previous years. In response to recent terror attacks, police have implemented strict security measures, including armed patrols and a zero-tolerance policy on drugs and pyrotechnics.

Australia took control of the second Test against Pakistan at the MCG, securing key wickets through Jackson Bird and Nathan Lyon despite only managing 50.5 overs due to weather interruptions. Pakistan captain Azhar Ali contributed a crucial half-century, passing 1,000 Test runs in 2016, but the innings ended with the hosts leading the three-Test series 1-0.

The 33-year-old forward has been limited to two appearances for Leicester City this season, despite a goal contribution for his parent club last season. He joined the 13th-pled Sheffield Wednesday prior to their Championship match against Norwich City.

Dave Baker, of the Olympus Trust, warned that the government cuts could be "crisis point" and the trust could be forced to make from September. The DfE spokesman said new funding plans would increase the trust's budget by 2.4%. The consultation on the new formula runs until 22 March 2017.
A teenage pedestrian was struck by a Ford Focus in Oldgate Lane, Rotherham, on Saturday. The driver was unharmed, and police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

Australia took a 1-0 lead in the series after rain and poor light halted play on day two of the second Test at the MCG. Despite only 50.5 overs being bowled, Australia claimed regular wickets, including the dismissals of Younus Khan and Misbah-ul-Haq, to leave Pakistan struggling at 111 for 5. Azhar Ali's half-century was the highlight for the visitors before the match was called off.

North Korea has restarted operations at the Yongbyon nuclear reactor, declaring it ready to face U.S. hostility with nuclear weapons. The White House warns Pyongyang to focus on fulfilling international obligations rather than advancing its nuclear program. Experts remain skeptical of North Korea's capabilities, noting the program's unclear status despite previous provocations and stalled six-party talks.

Irish Prime Minister Enda Kenny suggested that a potential referendum on Irish unity could occur if Brexit negotiations trigger a clear majority desire to join the Republic. While supporters like Gerry Adams welcomed the possibility as an opportunity for unification, unionist politicians dismissed the comments as "mischaneous" and unlikely to happen. Critics argued that the priority should remain on managing the economic impacts of Brexit rather than discussing border polls.

Canadian police detained ten individuals at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport and confiscated their passports, though no charges have been filed as investigations continue. Public Safety Minister Steven Blaney praised the officers' vigilance in addressing the global terror threat, while the families of the suspects have been informed and are struggling to understand the situation. This incident occurs against the backdrop of Canada's ongoing military involvement in the coalition against IS militants in Iraq and Syria.

Following a recent injury sustained during a match against Exeter, 26-year-old player Benjamin is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the season. Despite a history of injury struggles, Director of rugby Richard Cockerill confirmed that the injury is not serious and a full recovery is expected within eight to ten weeks. Meanwhile, the club also announced that scrum-half Sam Harrison has signed a new contract.

World number two Shaun Bingham's participation in the upcoming tournament depends on whether his wife gives birth before his first-round match against Joe Perry. While his wife is supportive of him playing, Bingham noted that he will need to consult with her once the baby arrives.

The Olympus Trust has warned that severe government funding cuts have pushed its schools to a "crisis point," leading to potential measures such as shortened school days, job cuts, and increased class sizes. While the Department for Education claims new funding plans will increase the trust's budget, unions and parents argue that the proposed changes fail to address the reality of declining spending power. The trust's leadership stated that these "unthinkable" decisions may become necessary by September to manage the financial deficit.
After a successful trial with the Shakers, 23-year-old defender Wes Brown has signed with Bury. He is expected to be available for the club's League One season opener against Doncaster this Saturday.

The City of Edinburgh Council has reported a cyber attack on its website service provider that resulted in the theft of users' email addresses. Officials have notified the relevant authorities and implemented extra security measures, warning that affected individuals may see an increase in spam or phishing attempts.

Kingston Maurward College and Weymouth College have been awarded significant grants for their respective building refurbishment projects. These investments, part of a national-wide funding scheme, aim to provide first-rate facilities to support high-quality teaching and learning.

The National Museum of the Royal Navy proposes to relocate the historic Yomper statue from Eastney to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard to facilitate larger visitor numbers. Local campaigners and the Portsmouth City Council have strongly opposed the move, arguing that the memorial belongs to Eastney and its historical context.

The museum director stated that a final decision has not yet been made, as they are currently considering all public comments submitted during the consultation process.

Stratfor's satellite imagery reveals that ISIS has systematically destroyed Mosul airport's runways and infrastructure to deny Iraqi forces a critical logistical asset, rendering the site nearly unusable for approaching troops. The destruction, which mirrors the group's tactics at Qayyarah air base, serves both to clear defensive sightlines and make repair efforts significantly more difficult than at previous sites. While the sugar factory remains intact as a testament to ISIS's utility, the group's scorched-earth strategy at Mosul airport represents a major setback for coalition forces attempting to reclaim the city.

Police are appealing for witnesses after an incident occurred near Corbett Place and Calais View on Thursday morning. They are urging anyone who saw a man in his late teens or early 20s, described as having dark, curly hair and wearing a dark top, to come forward.

Pawel Sroka, 33, has been charged in the murder of his 29-year-old partner, Joanna Trojniak, after a post-mort examination confirmed the cause of death as a stab wound to the chest. Ms Trojniak's next of kin have been informed. Mr Sroka is due to appear at Bromley Magistrates' Court on 4 April.

Jonas Gutiérrez revealed he was diagnosed with cancer last year, underwent surgery and chemotherapy, and made a emotional return to Newcastle United as a substitute in a defeat to Manchester United. He expressed his determination to prove he can still be a Premier League player while focusing on his recovery and future at the club.

British rowers Cassells and Scrimgeour secured their spot in the lightweight pairs final with the fastest qualifying time, defending their title from last year. Meanwhile, Irish Olympic silver medallist Paul O'Donovan advanced to the lightweight single sculls final after winning his semi-final, and his brother Mark O'Donovan along with partner Shane O'Driscol also qualified for the lightweight pairs final. The Rotterdam championships features both Olympic and non-Olympic classes, with finals scheduled for Saturday.

The world's largest clothing retailer, Inditex, reported a significant increase in net earnings and sales during the period ending July. This growth is driven by the expansion of its online stores and technological investments, such as mobile payment platforms.

The company's strategic focus on digital growth and international expansion sets it apart from competitors facing challenges due to unseasonal weather.

The Old Low Light Heritage Centre in North Shields hosts "From Dark to Light," the first major exhibition in his hometown dedicated to the artist Victor Noble Rainbird. The collection features previously unseen works, including paintings of the North Sea and poignant wartime drawings from his service on the Western Front. Running from 1 July to 6 September, the exhibition aims to shed new light on the life and legacy of this remarkable artist.

Jeremy Corbyn proposes a complete abolition of university tuition fees in England, as part of a bold "all-or-nothing" strategy aimed at appealing to younger voters and ensuring education is not detered by cost. The plan, which also reinstates maintenance grants, is estimated to cost £11.2bn annually, though independent analysts suggest the true expense to the Treasury may be lower. This shift marks a significant departure from previous Labour policies, effectively dismanting the current system of loans and repayments in favor of direct government funding for universities.

A bird became stuck in a wire fence while chasing a wood pigeon. RSPCA Inspector Mike Pugh freed the animal, who described it as as "The buzzard was feisty, but luckily, had not had much feather damage." and he released it back to the wild where he belongs.

Martyn Irvine has been named the BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year following his historic achievements in track cycling. The 28-year-old became the first Irish cyclist in 117 years to win a world title, while also securing a silver medal and a World Cup gold this year.

Prison Link Cymru warns that some ex-offenders are living rough for up to a year before finding suitable accommodation, while charity workers argue that investment in housing would be more cost-effective than re-incarcerating homeless repeat offenders. The Welsh Government maintains that more people are receiving help with housing issues than ever before, despite recent legislative changes that removed priority status for prison leavers.

Great Britain's men's basketball team will face Greece in a friendly match at London's Copper Box as they prepare for the upcoming FIBA EuroBasket. This game serves as Britain's final home fixture before they travel to Poland and Turkey for their final warm-up matches and tournament qualifiers.

The Campaign to Protect Rural England is seeking a judicial review against the £21.5m Castle Mill development in Oxford, arguing that the university failed to conduct a proper environmental impact assessment. While critics claim the five-story buildings spoil the historic skyline and harm the nearby Site of Special Scientific Interest, the University of Oxford maintains that mitigation measures are adequate and plans to occupy the completed flats by October. The case will be heard by a High Court judge on 23 October, with the city council currently conducting an independent review of the controversy.

Emily Thornberry stated Labour would not "frusterate Brexit" even if it failed to amend the bill. Ten shadow ministers were among 47 Labour MPs who rejected party orders to back it last week. Shadow chancellor John McDonnell said frontbenchers would have to quit if they defied the whip at the next vote. The draft legislation comes back to the Commons on Monday for three days of debate culminating in a vote on its third reading. Gurpal Virdi, 56, was acquitted by the jury at Southwark Crown Court after Mr Virdi had denied indectly assaulting a male prisoner and misconduct in public office. The charges dated back to on or before 7 November 1986. During the trial Mr Virdi accused the Metropolitan Police of bringing the criminal case against him as part of a 17-year campaign to "hound" him out of the force. The retired detective claimed the police had tried to discredit him after he gave evidence to the Stephen Lawrence inquiry about racism

The proposed merger between France's Essilor and Italy's Luxottica will create a massive industry behemoth, combining the world's leading lens and frame manufacturing.

The deal aims to generate significant innovation and synergies, but it has sparked concerns regarding potential antitrust issues and market dominance.

Industry experts warn that the merger could lead to a monopoly, potentially reducing consumer choice and quality while squeezing out smaller competitors.

The 2016 Hyundai Mercury Music Prize nominees were announced, with artists like Radiohead and Bowie being among the shortlisted candidates. The ceremony, which will follow a public vote and a judges' decision, is scheduled to take place at the Hammersmith Apollo.

Queen's University will cutting 1,100 undergraduate student places over the next three years to respond to an £8m cut in government subsidy. The cuts will come into effect from September 2015, and the university aims to reduce the number of student places by 1,100 over the next three years. The BBC understands that there are no immediate plans to close departments or courses, but that the cuts in funding may put some departments and courses at risk. The 2016 Hyundai Mercury Prize will take on September 15 at the Hammersmith Apollo, featuring a lineup of nominees such as Radiohead and the acts associated with David Bowie's *Blackstar*. The ceremony will feature a public vote to select a finalist, followed by a panel of judges choosing the overall winner.

Former Manchester United forward Dwight Yorke has revealed he is not fit to travel to Barcelona for a legends game due to complications from kidney failure, crediting his 28-year-old nephew Alexander with a "noble" donor transplant. While Yorke has made significant physical improvements since his 2015 illness, he remains some way off full fitness and is focusing on recovery ahead of potentially playing in a similar match next year. He also echoed Alan Shearer's view that English clubs are currently a long way off challenging Europe's elite for the Champions League.

Olympic silver medallist Nicole Houvenaghel has accused British Cycling of "ageism" and a "win-at-all-costs" culture following a leaked report into the organization's failures. The report suggests that the pursuit of medals came at the expense of athlete welfare, leading to claims that investigations into misconduct were previously "sanised." British Cycling has since admitted to these governance failings and implemented a 39-point action plan to address cultural shortcomings.

Johnston came through Kilmarnock's youth ranks to make the Premiership side's first team. Barr, 30, had been at Stark's Park for three seasons after leaving Airdrieonians and played 17 times as Reros dropped to League One. The 29-year-old Stewart joined Rers at the same time, from Derry City, and scored five times in 36 appearances last season.

The Leith Walk by-election marked the first use of the Single Transferable Vote system to elect two members in a single ward, resulting in an SNP victory for John Lewis Ritchie and a Scottish Labour win for Marion Donaldson. The election was triggered by the resignations of outgoing SNP MP Deidre Brock and Green MSP Maggie Chapman, with turnout recorded at 25.1%. Additionally, the SNP retained the Midlothian West seat, securing a victory for Kelly Parry following the departure of Owen Thompson.

The obituary of Meles Zenawi reflects the complex legacy of the former Ethiopian leader, whose rule was characterized by a tension between revolutionary ideals and autocratic reality. While his administration drove significant economic growth and infrastructure development, it also faced criticism for failing to address systemic poverty and for suppressing political dissent.

His death leaves a power-vacuum in the Horn of Africa, raising fears of regional instability as his era of influence shifts toward a contested and uncertain future.

The Republican presidential debate focused on immigration, healthcare, and outreach to Latino voters, which eventually devolved into a period of personal insults and shouting. The candidates, particularly Senator Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz, launched heavy attacks against Donald Trump, questioning his business record, conservative credentials, and policy details.

The debate highlighted the tension between traditional political tactics and the desire for authenticity, as with Trump being on his heels for much of the evening.

The charity Prison Link Cymru warns that ex-offenders can become long-term homeless due to a lack of suitable accommodation following their release. Workers argue that investing in stable housing would be more cost-effective than the cycle of re-revolving offenders into the prison system.

With the "chronic" need for housing, advocates suggest that increasing one-bedroom properties can help prevent the cycle of homelessness and recidism.

Nigel Farage's former deputy, Suzanne Evans, announced that she will not stand in the UKIP leadership election despite her six-month suspension, which she claims is politically motivated to prevent her candidacy. Evans has instead thrown her support behind councillor Lisa Duffy, arguing that the party must shed its "hard-right" image and undergo significant internal reform. Evans stated that while she would "very much like" to run, party leadership has effectively blocked her path through what she describes as an abuse of the rulebook.

Researchers investigating an Ebola outbreak in Guineaé traced the index case to Emile, a boy who played in a hollowed tree struck by fruit bats. The team found the tree had recently burned, causing a "rain of bats," and villagers had collected the insects for food. While bushmeat was ruled out as the source, scientists believe Emile’s exposure to bat droppings in the tree triggered the infection.

Two supporters who cut themselves off from a stadium tour were discovered during a security sweep at Old Trafford and handed over to police, who decided not to arrest them. Manchester United confirmed that the pair posed no risk to attendees of the Arsenal game, noting they had already passed through standard security checks. This incident follows a similar scare six months ago when a fake explosive device caused the cancellation of a match against Bournemouth.

A study published in the journal *Cell* suggests that a "fasting-mimicking diet" can reverse diabetes symptoms by regenerating insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. By cycling between five days of low-calorie eating and 25 days of normal eating, researchers were able to trigger a cellular reprogramming that restored organ function in mice. Experts believe these findings could lead to significant new treatments for both type 1 and type 2 diabetes without the need for genetic alterations.

Police are investigating a targeted shooting involving a dark-colored car near two primary schools in Liverpool, though no injuries were reported. While students and staff were ordered to stay indoors as a precaution, school officials confirmed that pupils remained safe and the school day continued as planned.

Former Sussex cricketer Anyon Seamer has been appointed as the new head coach of the women's senior side, as he also will lead the under-19 and under-21 teams. He succeeds Charlotte Burton and will work alongside Alexia Walker, who moves into a role supporting the senior, under-21, and under-19 squads.

Olympic silver medallist Joanna Houvenaghel has accused British Cycling of "ageism" and prioritizing medals over athlete welfare following a leaked report detailing the organization's cultural failings. The report suggests that previous investigations into sexism were sanitized, prompting British Cycling to implement a 39-point action plan to address these systemic issues. This comes as part of a broader scrutiny of the "win-at-all-costs" culture within British sport.

A power outage at Lancaster's Caton Road substation affected approximately 53,000 properties, causing significant disruption to travel, education, and local services. Power was restored to the remaining 10,000 affected customers by 16:30 BST, though the specific cause of the failure remains unknown. The incident led to widespread operational challenges, including traffic light failures and closures for several key institutions like Lancaster University and the town hall.

The Alabama Securities Commission investigated Lee after her lawyer's allegations that she was manipulated into publishing a 88-year-old manuscript. The new work, "Go Set a Watchman," features an adult Scout Finch returning to Alabama, and sparked the probe after the New York Times reported requests from a doctor investigating whether Lee was capable of consenting to the release. Lee's lawyer claimed she was "extremely hurt" by the manipulation, while the commission's director stated she was satisfied with the investigation's outcome. Unions at BAE Systems have warned of potential delays to the Royal Navy's Type 26 frigate program, raising fears that up to 800 jobs could be lost if commitments are not met. While Scottish political leaders from the SNP, Labour, and Liberal Democrats expressed deep concern over the uncertainty and called for guaranteed assurances, Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson insisted that the government has confirmed the original timetable and order numbers remain unchanged.

Doull earned Olympic redemption to add to the four Welsh silver medallists in Rio, alongside Sir Bradley Wiggins, Steven Burke and Ed Clancy to beat the world champions. "That was just surreal, it feels dreamlike" said the Cardiff rider. "We've been in situations like that before when we've been so close and have lost so to pull it off now is unbelievable."

Entering the final event of the Gotzis Hypo-Meeting, Olympic champion Jessica Ennis-Hill sits in third place with 5,544 points. She remains on track to qualify for both the Rio Olympics and the World Championships, provided she meets her target scoring thresholds in the 800m.

Exitor City reported a total profit of £1.642m for 204-5, primarily driven from the sale of midfielder Matt Grimes to Swansea City. This financial surplus follows a period where the club required an emergency loan to cover player wages.

The club's board has agreed that the transfer income will be used to improve infrastructure and club strength, including plans to redevelop St James Park.

The City of Edinburgh Council has reported a cyberattack on its website service provider that resulted in the theft of users' email addresses. While council services remained unaffected, officials have warned the public to watch for an increase in spam and phishing attempts. The incident has been reported to the relevant authorities, and extra security measures have been implemented to prevent further issues.

An investigation into the closed Tawel Fan ward at Glan Clwyd Hospital has revealed that at least seven patients' families were informed that inadequate care may have contributed to their deaths. While the Betsi Cadwaladr health board acknowledges these findings and is conducting a thorough review, relatives remain frustrated by the lack of accountability and the delay in publishing the mortality report. The scandal has already placed the health board under special government supervision, with further reports expected later this year to determine the full extent of the failures.

Ireland defeated Zimbabwe by three wickets in Bangkok to maintain their 100% record in Group B of the World Twenty20 qualifiers. The Joyce twins starred in the victory, with Isobel taking four wickets and Cecilia scoring 36, as Ireland chased down Zimbabwe's total of 78.

After a mix-up involving a mistaken tool collection, Andrew Bickel became an instant viral celebrity due his unique, humorous story. He joked that he would donate to a dog charity shop rather than a cat shop, noting he has enjoyed the brief moment of fame.

On August 22, a vintage Hawker Hunter jet crashed into traffic on the A27 in West Sussex, killing eleven people. Fire crews face a "extremely challenging" recovery operation as they work to thank those killed and injured. Police have finished scene work on the A27, though investigations continue as they attempt to determine the cause of the crash, which involves pilot Andy Hill.

Following the tragic plane crash that killed 71 people, survivors including Chapecoense defender Helio Hermito Zampier Neto are in stable condition after undergoing multiple surgeries. Investigations suggest the aircraft ran out of fuel, as the pilot reportedly proceeded with the flight despite warnings regarding fuel levels. In response to the tragedy, Bolivia has suspended the operating license of the charter airline LaMia while authorities work to determine responsibility for the crash.

Retten detective Gurpal Virdi, 56, was acquitted by the jury at Southwark Crown Court on charges of indeently assaulting a male prisoner and misconduct in public office. The charges dated back to on or before 7 November 1986. During the trial Mr Virdi accused the Metropolitan Police of bringing the criminal case against him as part of a 17-year campaign to "hound" him out of the force.

The latest live-action "Cinderella" directed by Kenneth Branagh has become a box office success, grossing $70 million in its U.S. opening weekend. The film distinguishes itself by remaining largely faithful to the classic animated original, with Lily James starring as a proactive Cinderella who makes active choices rather than passively waiting for rescue. Despite critics noting its traditional "preserved-in-amber" romance, the cast and crew argue that the film's commitment to the source material is precisely what resonates with modern audiences.

Exeter City reported a £1.642m profit for 2014-15, primarily driven by the sale of Matt Grimes to Swansea City for a club-record £1.75m. The financial success came despite the club facing a transfer embargo and an emergency loan to cover wages earlier that year.
